title: Coordination fix for split-stream fallback causing duplicated partial outputs and client confusion
creator: Aisha Menon
description:
Summary: Several customers reported duplicated partial transcripts and confusing reordered tokens when their clients experienced network hiccups and the request was routed to a fallback pool (hosted -> dedicated variant or cross-region). The visible symptom was clients receiving two overlapping partial results: a truncated earlier segment followed by a late chunk that replays overlapping tokens. Impact: multiple active customers saw degraded UX, some aborted request flows, and a support escalation to SE and Customer Success. Scope was limited to streaming (SSE) requests that triggered fallback routing under transient edge errors and concurrent reconnections.

Reproduction steps:
1) Start a long-running streaming generation over SSE through Hosted API (preferred model heavy tail: 16k context).
2) Simulate edge partition (drop long-lived idle TCP) and trigger reconnection logic in client.
3) Force the server routing layer to failover the request to a different pool (e.g., hosted->dedicated or region fallback) while a partial KV cache exists and the old connection had emitted a tail chunk but not final commit.
4) Observe duplicate overlapping fragments: client receives both the original tail chunk (late commit) and a resumed stream that replays recent tokens.

Root cause hypothesis (confirmed by traces and kernel logs): race between fallback orchestration and session fencing. When the primary stream suffers a disconnect, the routing layer attempts a best-effort handoff: it creates a new session on the fallback runtime but reuses the same ephemeral session token without atomic transfer of the finalization marker. Due to eventual delivery of the last in-flight chunks from the original host (edge proxies retry), the client sees two sequences with overlapping token ranges. There was no robust idempotency marker across pool boundaries and our per-session finalizer did not guarantee at-most-once semantic in fallback scenarios.

Design decision / Trade-offs considered:
- Strict global session locks: would guarantee no duplicates but require cross-pool coordination and hurt tail latency. Rejected for short-term fix.
- Always-preferring deterministic server-side dedupe by checksum ranges: lower latency impact, incremental, and easier to canary. Selected as primary remediation.
- Centralized commit log for session finalization: ideal long-term for cross-pool correctness but requires infra work and migration. Scoped to roadmap for Q3.

Planned fixes (short-term -> medium-term):
1) Introduce session boundaries with cross-pool idempotency keys (opaque final_token_id) that get embedded in stream events. Runtime change: accept final_token_id and drop any late segments that duplicate an already-committed token range.
2) Add per-chunk range checksum and token-index metadata so clients and servers can perform local dedupe. This will be additive to SSE payloads (backwards-compatible: servers can emit both new metadata and legacy events).
3) Update routing layer to delay final handoff until a short safepoint is reached or to mark the original session as orphaned and signal proxies to stop re-emitting late chunks. This keeps latency costs bounded by a small safepoint window (100-500ms tunable).
4) Instrumentation: new Grafana panels and per-request traces that show fallback events, final_token_id collisions, and duplicate-chunk counts.

Testing and rollout plan:
- Unit tests for dedupe logic and token-range checksums (runtime repo).
- Integration test that simulates edge retries and cross-pool handoff in the testbed. Add to CI gating with a deterministic short-circuit mode.
- Canary: feature-flagged rollout at 5% routing traffic -> 25% -> 75% -> 100% across 48h windows. Start with internal tenants and a handful of impacted customers included in the first canary ring.
- Rollback: feature flag off and immediate revert of runtime behavior; fallback to earlier routing behavior. Ensure monitoring alarms trigger on duplicate-chunk regressions.

Customer communications and mitigations:
- Support runbook added: how to detect duplicate partial outputs, steps for temporary client-side mitigation (apply client-side last-seen-token filter), and how to collect traces.
- Sent interim update to impacted customers on 2026-03-11 with mitigation suggestions and ETA for patch.

Owner and approvals: Diego to lead the runtime patch. Engineering managers (Kiran Patel) and PM (Marta Ruiz) reviewed and approved the short-term approach on 2026-03-12. Security reviewed the metadata changes; no secrets introduced.

Longer-term work (follow-up tickets): cross-pool commit log, stronger SLA around routing handoff, and a migration path to server-side global finalizers. These are scoped as runtime-2026 Q3 initiatives.
comments: 2026-03-10 Aisha Menon: Filed after two escalations from mid-market customers — transcript samples and customer logs attached in links. Tagged oncall and alerted SE team.

2026-03-11 Diego Alvarez: Initial triage — repro produced locally by simulating edge proxy delayed ACK + routing failover. Observed duplicated ranges 0..N and N-3..N in client trace. Hypothesis added to ticket.
2026-03-12 Kiran Patel (EM): Reviewed options. Recommend incremental server-side dedupe and a short safepoint delay. Decision recorded and PM/Design loop closed.
2026-03-12 Marta Ruiz (PM): Confirmed we should prioritize low-latency option for customers with strict tail latency. Approve canary plan and customer communication drafts.
2026-03-13 Diego Alvarez: Drafted runtime PR with idempotency key plumbing and per-chunk checksum metadata. Running unit tests locally; integration job queued.

2026-03-14 QA (Santiago): Integration test uncovered edge case where fallback replays with different quantization variant causing checksum mismatches even when duplicates exist. Added follow-up: normalize tokenization before checksum.
